correctness.rationale: Over an arbitrary commutative base algebra, preservation of \([a_1,a_2]=a_2\) forces the first-column coefficient \(D=0\), \((A-1)E=0\), and \(F=BE\); preservation of \([a_2,a_2]=a_3\) gives \(G=H=0\), \(I=E^2\). Invertibility makes \(A,E\) units, hence \(A=1\), and \([a_1,a_1]=\lambda a_3\) gives exactly \(B^2=\lambda(E^2-1)\). Thus the displayed coordinate ring represents the automorphism functor. After adjoining \(s^2=\lambda\), fresh symbolic reduction in characteristic two gives \((b+s(u-1))^2-\lambda(u^2-1)=v^2\); the hypersurface has dimension two and a nonzero square-zero class in every geometric local ring, hence is nowhere smooth. Dual numbers impose no first-order relation, giving tangent dimension three, exactly matching the independently published derivation matrices.
residual_risks: The result concerns only the L8(lambda) family and not a smoothness classification of all sixteen three-dimensional Leibniz types.
